tier1.why: available in THREE external datasets (MyoKi, KIN-MUS, KINE-ADL) and the MCP and PIP flexion groups each passed a per-subject physical anchor in 22/22 subjects (median +17.79 deg for MCP, +13.08 deg for PIP, reaching -> manipulation)

tier2.why: the thumb channels: identity and unit are clear, the thumb MCP+IP anchor passed 18/22 subjects (0.818, just above the 0.80 threshold) and the CMC flexion anchor 22/22, but thumb_cmc_flexion exists in only TWO external datasets (MyoKi has no thumb CMC flexion channel at all) and the whole thumb CMC complex carries the nomenclature caveat the KINE-ADL paper itself raises
tier2.recommendation: admit only if the downstream task genuinely needs the thumb; otherwise ship tier 1 alone

CommonPoseSubset_v2_candidate.rationale: the frozen plan prefers 8 trustworthy DOFs over 16 semantically confused ones; the pivot here is the four MCP flexions and the four PIP flexions, the only channels in the UJI corpus that passed a per-subject physical anchor in every subject
CommonPoseSubset_v2_candidate.restriction_that_travels_with_every_memb: numeric coordinate equivalence between datasets is UNVERIFIED for every member; only semantic correspondence is established
